subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approval timing, term options, and onboarding MAP
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cloudwave.io>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.io, emily.summers@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer questions — term length and approval windows

Irene — thanks for sending the term options. A few quick clarifying Qs from procurement: 1) Does AWS Marketplace private offer support a blended commitment + overage model? 2) Our legal is pushing back on any auto-renew clause longer than 12 months without an explicit opt-in. 3) Who signs the private offer on our side — legal or procurement?

We want to avoid a long signature loop; happy to expedite if you can provide a short mutual action plan and a recommended term with justification. Also looped Emily from AWS as she mentioned some buyer-approval gating we should expect.

Best,
Samir Kapoor
Head of Cloud Ops — CloudWave
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cloudwave.io>, emily.summers@amazon.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer questions — term length and approval windows

Samir — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and a path forward: 

- Blended model: yes — Redwood can structure a private offer that combines a committed monthly minimum and metered overage pricing. See attached sheet (RDW_PrivateOffer_Term_Options_v3.xlsx) with three proposals: 12m standard, 24m discount, 36m enterprise discount. Each row shows committed spend, overage rate, and unit economics.
- Auto-renew: we can remove auto-renew and make the offer require explicit signature/renewal at term end. 
- Signature: technically procurement signs, but we commonly ask legal to countersign in parallel to avoid serial handoffs.

Proposed MAP to speed approval: 
1) Week 0 (this week): Redwood provides final terms + one-page SOW and MAP (attached draft).
2) Week 1: CloudWave procurement confirms preferred term (12/24/36) and provides buyer approval matrix (who signs, internal thresholds).
3) Week 2: AWS partner manager (Emily) confirms private offer readiness in marketplace and reserves negotiation window.
4) Week 3: Signature + onboarding kickoff.

If CloudWave needs an internal approver ladder, Ben can draft a short buyer approval matrix template you can drop in. Vanessa — can you own the offer creation with AWS once we have the selected row? Lauren — please confirm there are no legal redlines in the draft MAP that would block a 2-week timeline. Emily — any constraints from AWS on reserving private-offer windows for this timeline?

Irene Choi
Head of Strategic GTM — Redwood Inference
From: Emily Summers <emily.summers@amazon.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cloudwave.io>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer questions — term length and approval windows

Thanks all — from the Marketplace side a couple of things to flag: 
- We can lock a private-offer reservation for up to 14 calendar days while terms are finalized; beyond that the buyer will need to re-request.
- For blended commit + usage, ensure the offer clearly states the committed minimum SKU and the metering SKU for overage. We will validate marketplace schema during creation; Redwood must provide SKU mapping.
- Buyer approvals: AWS does not sign on behalf of the buyer; the buyer must sign or grant delegated signatory rights. If CloudWave needs to split procurement vs legal approvals, we recommend they provide the approval matrix to the Partner Manager (me) so we can note expected ETA in our intake.

I can hold a 1-hr slot Thu for the MAP walkthrough if that helps.

—Emily
Senior Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cloudwave.io>, emily.summers@amazon.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer questions — term length and approval windows

Samir — looping in the exact term rows we recommend based on CloudWave's sizing notes. TL;DR recommendation: go with a 24-month commit with explicit non-auto-renew and a month-to-month overage SKU. That gives CloudWave ~18% effective discount vs 12m while keeping your legal comfort on renewal. 

Next steps for you:
- Please complete the attached buyer approval matrix with names + thresholds (procurement@cloudwave.io if easier). Ben will use that to fill the HubSpot deal and create the private-offer request in our backend.
- If procurement needs a one-line justification for finance: "24m commit optimized for predictable unit cost while preserving flexibility via metered overage."

Attaching the MAP draft (CloudWave-MAP-draft.pdf) and the term sheet workbook. I’ll start the private-offer draft in parallel and will add Emily as partner contact when ready.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: pasted from: On Wed, 14 Mar 2028 at 11:43 AM Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cloudwave.io> wrote:
> Irene / Vanessa / Emily — thanks for the clear plan. Two quick clarifications from procurement:
>
> 1) Can you include a one-paragraph data residency and retention statement in the MAP draft? Our security team needs that to start their review in parallel.
> 2) Who is the Redwood signatory on the private offer — we need a name on the signature block so our procurement can triage to the right approver.
>
> I’ll have our procurement contact (procurement@cloudwave.io) fill the approval matrix by EOD Friday.
>
> Samir

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cloudwave.io>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer questions — buyer approval timing and signature

Samir — we can add a short data-residency blurb to the MAP (US-only region, standard retention 90 days for logs, customer data stored in your account by default). For signature: Redwood signs via our Head of Revenue Ops for private offers under $250k ARR; for anything above that the signatory is VP of Commercial (Irene can confirm). I’ll add a named signatory block to the draft.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@cloudwave.io>, emily.summers@amazon.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer questions — buyer approval timing and signature

Samir — confirming the plan and next asks: 
1) Redwood named signatory (if below $250k ARR): Ben Carter, Head Sales Ops. If CLW prefers Irene as signatory, we can accommodate but it will add a day for internal approvals.
2) Vanessa will update the MAP with a 1-paragraph data residency and retention note and reattach.
3) Procurement matrix expected EOD Friday — once we receive that, Vanessa & Ben will submit the private-offer draft to AWS and Emily will reserve the 14-day window.

If we get procurement matrix Friday, target signature week of Mar 26 and onboarding kickoff Mar 29. If CloudWave wants a faster cadence, flag now and we’ll move Irene into signatory review to compress one day.

Thanks — Irene
Head of Strategic GTM — Redwood Inference
